newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen wants more money from Krupp - report.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen wants more money from Krupp - report.

text.p: German industrial group Thyssen AG is demanding that Krupp pay an additional 500 million marks in connection with the recent merger of their steel operations, the news magazine Der Spiegel reported.
In an advance copy of an article to be published in its Monday edition, Spiegel said Krupp was refusing to pay the additional settlement, and that the merger could collapse.
Spokesmen for the two companies, however, said the discussions about the merger were on track.
"Everything else is groundless speculation," a Krupp spokesman said.
"There is no question of the talks collapsing," a Thyssen spokesman said.
The two groups merged their steel operations on April 1 in Thyssen Krupp Stahl AG KFHG.F, in which Krupp holds a 40 percent share and Thyssen 60 percent.
The deal calls for Thyssen Krupp to pay Thyssen 300 million marks a year of its profit through 2001.
